data:
Runink PULSE (the Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine) is Runink’s marketing-analysis application. You give it a website. It audits the site, writes a multichannel diagnosis, and turns that diagnosis into a working plan: draft content waiting for approval, a draft campaign, a 30-day follow-up cycle, market research, audience profiles, and leads.
Every AI step runs on the platform’s own inference server (mistral.rs’s mistralrs-server). PULSE calls no third-party LLM API.
Getting startedSign in, set your business profile, and run your first Site Audit. User guideThe marketing loop, screen by screen: audit, audience, create, publish, follow up. Brand and connectionsBusiness profile, content defaults, and the accounts and data sources PULSE reads. Admin guideDeployment, configuration, users, publishing controls, billing, and the site pipeline. Developer guideBuild, test, regenerate protos, and call the gRPC API. API referenceEvery gRPC service and method, derived from the .proto files. ConceptsOne port, sovereign inference, the judging ladder, agent activity. Agent model cardsWhat each AI agent does, reads, and produces, and where it stops. TroubleshootingReal error messages and what to do about each one.

data.what-pulse-is-and-what-it-is-not#What PU:
PULSE is application code only: a Go gRPC backend (grpc/) and a Flutter client (flutter/) for web, Linux, and Android. The platform around it lives in other Runink repositories:
Runink TIDE runs the deploy and dev loop (the tide CLI; core still works as an alias), the operator that reconciles a PULSE instance, the shared model weights, and the native inference builds. The extracted libraries security, mesh, inference, store, and ui supply authentication, interceptors and self-healing, the inference engine wrappers, persistence, and the shared Billing, Profile, Admin, and Data sources pages. The API is gRPC. Browsers reach it over gRPC-Web on the same port. There is no REST API for campaigns, content, or leads. A few plain HTTP endpoints exist (health, sign-in, media, voice, the podcast feed, A2A); the API reference lists every one.

This guide is for the people who deploy and operate a PULSE instance.
Configuration referenceEvery environment variable the backend reads, grouped by purpose. Users and accessBreak-glass admin, Google sign-in, seeded roles, and the Admin page. Publishing controlsThe kill switch and per-channel arming for everything outward-facing. Site pipelineBlog posts to your Hugo site, the daily site audit, and audit-fix PRs. BillingThe shared Billing page, fed by the operator’s subscription variables and PULSE’s usage ledger. Plans and compute unitsLite, Dedicated, and Enterprise; compute units as model-slot time; currency and billing periods. Telephony and messagingAsterisk cold calls, browser voice, and the WhatsApp/SMS edge. OperationsHealth, self-healing, TLS, logging, rate limits, and the licence gate.
data.first-things-to-set#First things to set: Setting Why PULSE_JWT_SECRET Required. The server will not start without it. CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK Required. The database refuses to open without it, rather than write OAuth tokens in plaintext. TENANT_ID Names the tenant for billing, the profile page, and the Admin page. PULSE_WEB_DIR or CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Serve the app same-origin, or pin the origins that may call the API. INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL, INFERENCE_MODEL Point at the shared inference plane, and name the model it serves. The full list is in the configuration reference.
data.one-instance-per-deployment#One instance: SQLite has one writer, so each deployment runs one backend instance. In a cluster, Litestream replicates the database to the in-cluster object store. TIDE’s operator refuses any other object-store endpoint.
data.serving-the-web-app#Serving the web app: Set PULSE_WEB_DIR to the Flutter web build, and the backend serves the app itself, on the same origin as the API. Then no CORS configuration is needed.
data.what-this-repository-ships#What this rep:
The backend image, built from grpc/Dockerfile with the repository root as the build context. The build is self-contained. It:
Builds the Flutter web bundle, with CanvasKit bundled locally instead of fetched from a CDN, and with no source maps. Clones the sibling repositories that grpc/go.mod points at, using a short-lived token passed as a build argument. Compiles a static, cgo-free Go server. The SQLite driver (modernc.org/sqlite) needs no C toolchain. The runtime image is debian:bookworm-slim with:
ffmpeg, for assembling video creatives. chromium, for every feature that reads live web pages: the Site Audit, lead prospecting, and market signals. Litestream, pinned by SHA-256, with its schedule in grpc/litestream.yml. Voice transcription is not in the image. Like the text model, it runs as a separate service that PULSE reaches through VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL. Neither is text-to-speech: PULSE speaks through TIDE’s shared ttsd (TTSD_URL).
data.who-deploys-pulse#Who deploys PULSE:
Runink TIDE does. This repository holds application code and the backend image build. Cluster bring-up, the operator, and deploys all live in TIDE:
cd ../core/grpc # TIDE's Go module go run ./cmd/core deploy pulse TIDE’s pulse-operator reconciles the instance into the pulse-system namespace. The operator’s custom resource is the authoritative pod spec, so change the resource or its overlay, not the live Deployment. Deploys are plain kustomize.

data: System → Billing (/billing) is the shared Runink Billing page from org-runink/ui. PULSE serves its API, runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService, over the org-runink/billing library, with PULSE-specific hooks. The page lists and prices PULSE’s own plans, never another product’s. For the plans, prices, and compute units themselves, see Plans and compute units.
data.the-deprecated-meteringservice#The depre:
pulse.v1.MeteringService is kept for one release as an alias. Its messages have no field for measured usage, so it reports none:
GetResourceUsage answers UNIMPLEMENTED, pointing to BillingService/GetOverview, which reports the measured usage. GetComputeBudget returns the tier, the seats, the seat-derived allowance, and the per-seat price. On Dedicated and Enterprise the allowance is left unset, because those plans are unmetered. Consumed and remaining units are always unset. SetComputeBudget always answers UNIMPLEMENTED. The allowance comes from paid seats. Without TENANT_ID, both reads answer FAILED_PRECONDITION: no subscription is on record for this deployment (TENANT_ID is not projected). New clients should call runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService/GetOverview.
data.what-each-part-of-the-page-does#What eac: Feature In PULSE Plan catalog and price quotes (ListPlans, QuotePlan) Work. Pricing is arithmetic, done on the server, from PULSE’s catalogue. Overview of your subscription (GetOverview) Works, from the variables above. Compute units Measured model-slot time for the viewer’s account. Dedicated and Enterprise show “unmetered”. Estimate Every line is either computed or says why it cannot be. A line that cannot be computed, such as overage with no billing period on record, leaves the estimate without a total. Currency The page shows US-dollar list prices and says so. Invoices are in your regional currency; see Currency and billing periods. Checkout and the billing portal (StartCheckout, OpenPortal) PULSE has no payment provider. Both answer “not configured”, so nothing on this page can charge. Subscriptions are bought through Runink. Seats (ListSeats, AssignSeat, RevokeSeat) PULSE keeps no seat roster. The page shows no seats section. Billing actions are logged to the process log as billing audit lines.
data.where-the-subscription-comes-from#Where:
PULSE runs one deployment per tenant. The subscription is read from environment variables that Runink TIDE’s operator projects onto the pod:
Variable Meaning When missing TENANT_ID The tenant No subscription on record SUBSCRIPTION_TIER The plan tier: lite, dedicated, or enterprise lite SUBSCRIPTION_SEATS Number of seats 1 SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS Subscription status active The tier, seat, and status defaults apply only when TENANT_ID is set. Without TENANT_ID, the page shows that no subscription is on record. It does not invent a Lite plan. An unknown tier is never treated as Lite: the subscription is shown as suspended.
The environment carries no billing period and no annual flag. The page therefore prices the month-to-month rate and shows no current period. A Dedicated plan is sold yearly only, so its seat line has no month-to-month price to show.
data.where-usage-comes-from#Where usage comes:
PULSE records compute as model-slot time, per paying account (see How PULSE records compute).
Setting Effect RUNINK_ACCOUNTS_FILE The member-to-purchaser file TIDE’s operator projects. PULSE uses it to find who pays for each signed-in person’s work. OBJECTSTORE_* (or the LITESTREAM_* object-store settings) Where the usage ledger is kept. It is the same object store the retrieval corpus uses. The Billing page reads usage for the viewer’s own purchaser account, the same key the usage was recorded under. When no object store is configured, usage is held in memory, and the page states that its window starts when the process started. It never prices a partial window as a whole period.

data: PULSE is configured through environment variables. This page lists the ones the backend reads, grouped by purpose. It names variables and describes their effect. It does not show values: secrets come from the secret store, and Runink TIDE’s operator projects the rest.
data.billing-and-tenancy#Billing and tenancy: Variable Effect TENANT_ID This deployment’s tenant. SUBSCRIPTION_TIER, SUBSCRIPTION_SEATS, SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS The subscription the Billing page shows. RUNINK_ACCOUNTS_FILE The member-to-purchaser file TIDE’s operator projects. Model-slot usage is recorded against the purchaser it names. Usage is kept on the object store configured under Storage. See Billing and Plans and compute units.
data.command-line#Command line: Command Meaning pulse-server serve Starts the backend. --port, -p The port to listen on. Defaults to PORT when set, otherwise 0, which picks a free port.
data.inference#Inference: Variable Effect INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL Use the shared inference plane at this address. Unset means PULSE starts its own mistralrs-server. INFERENCE_MODEL The model to request. Code default GLM-4-9B-Chat-Q4_K_M.gguf, which mistral.rs does not load (chatglm) — set a Qwen-family model. Must match what the server loads. INFERENCE_API_KEY Key for the inference server. INFERENCE_HOST, INFERENCE_IP, INFERENCE_PORT, MISTRAL_PORT Where a local inference child listens. BINARY_MISTRALRS_SERVER, MODEL_DIR, PULSE_AGENT_CONFIG The local engine binary, the model directory, and the agent config (default ./agents/pulse.ini). VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL The speech-to-text server. INFERENCE_DECODE_TOK_S The platform decode rate that generation budgets are sized from. TIDE injects it. PULSE_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS Wait allowed for the first token. Default 5 minutes. PULSE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Overrides the decode budget outright. PULSE_ADMIT_MAX, PULSE_ADMIT_QUEUE, PULSE_ADMIT_MODE, PULSE_ADMIT_WEIGHTS In-process admission control. Off unless PULSE_ADMIT_MAX is above zero. PULSE_GATE_MAX_INFLIGHT, PULSE_GATE_FIRST_TOKEN_SECONDS Cross-app admission gate for the shared plane. Off unless one is set. PULSE_DEDUP_TTL How long a repeated generation is reused. Go duration, default 1h. PULSE_JUDGEMENT off disables the judging ladder. PULSE_AUDIT_DEADLINE_SECONDS The end-to-end deadline of the diagnostic and the site audit. Default 170 (the owner’s three minutes, less the render). Clamped to 10–900. Every phase’s budget is derived from what is left of it; a phase that does not finish shows on the reasoning card as “not completed within the 3-minute budget” and the result says it is partial. PULSE_BRAIN_MAX_SEQS The brain tier’s --max-seqs. Default 2. Bounds how many judge claims run at once. INFERENCE_PREFILL_TOK_S, INFERENCE_PREFILL_EXPONENT The plane’s prefill curve. The diagnostic trims its prompt to what its phase can prefill. Set from the System76 benchmark. PULSE_RERANKER off ranks the prompt’s context lexically instead of asking the reranker tier (reranker through the model router). PULSE_EGRESS_ALL_AGENTS Screens every agent’s output, not only content agents. EMBEDDING_URL The embeddings endpoint for grounding. EMBEDDING_FORMAT qwen3-embedding (default), nomic-v1.5, or raw. Anything else stops the server. MODEL_EMBEDDING_DIM Vector width. Default 768. CORE_HEALTH_URL Where agent health reports go. Unset means no reports. See Sovereign inference.
data.media#Media: Variable Effect BINARY_VIDEO_CLI The video generation tool. Without it, video creatives, course videos, and the shorts engine are off. VIDEO_MODEL_DIR Model directory for video generation. FFMPEG_PATH Overrides the ffmpeg binary. ORPHEUS_BACKEND The compute backend passed to the video tool. Default vulkan.
data.names-that-are-no-longer-read#Names that:
Setting these does nothing. PULSE does not warn about them.
Every LLAMA_* variable, including LLAMA_MODEL and LLAMA_REMOTE_URL. Use INFERENCE_MODEL and INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL. SD_REMOTE_URL. The image-generation tier was retired. TTS_REMOTE_URL. Speech synthesis runs inside PULSE.
data.publishing#Publishing: Variable Effect PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED The global kill switch. Only the exact value true arms anything. PULSE_PUBLISH_ Narrows one channel: BLOG, PODCAST, AUDIOBOOK, YOUTUBE, INSTAGRAM, SPOTIFY, LINKEDIN. PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH, PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON The per-channel arming file, or the same JSON inline. PULSE_SITE_REPO, PULSE_SITE_BRANCH, PULSE_SITE_BLOG_DIR, PULSE_SITE_PUBLISH_MODE, PULSE_SITE_AUTHOR, PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL Blog publishing to your website. PULSE_GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, PULSE_GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL The author on commits PULSE makes. YOUTUBE_PRIVACY_STATUS public, unlisted, or private. Unset means private. LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN, LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN, LINKEDIN_API_VERSION The LinkedIn publisher’s token (from a secret), the member to post as, and the API version header. PULSE_PODCAST_TITLE, PULSE_PODCAST_DESCRIPTION, PULSE_PODCAST_LANGUAGE Podcast feed metadata. See Publishing controls and Site pipeline.
data.security#Security: Variable Effect PULSE_JWT_SECRET Required. The key that signs and verifies every session. There is no default. It must never be a value that has been committed anywhere. CORE_ENVELOPE_KEK Required. The key that seals OAuth tokens in the database. The database refuses to open without it. PULSE_TLS_CERT, PULSE_TLS_KEY In-process TLS for direct exposure. Set both or neither. TLS 1.2 minimum, forward-secret AEAD suites only. MESH_MTLS true requires mutual TLS on the listener, with rotating certificates from the shared mesh CA. Takes precedence over PULSE_TLS_*. TLS 1.3 only. MESH_CA_CERT, MESH_CA_KEY The mesh CA, from the secret store. Needed when MESH_MTLS=true. MESH_ADVERTISE_IP, MESH_ADVERTISE_HOST Extra IP and DNS names on the mesh certificate. LICENSE, LICENSE_FILE, LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY An offline licence, inline or as a file, and the key that verifies it. With no licence there is no gating.
data.server#Server: Variable Effect PORT Default for --port. PULSE_WEB_DIR Directory of the Flutter web build. When set, the backend serves the app on the same origin as the API. CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Comma-separated origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Unset means *. Only an exact listed origin gets credentials. PULSE_ENV production turns the insecure-configuration warnings into a refusal to start. See Operations. PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION true turns on gRPC reflection. Off by default. For local work only. PULSE_RATE_RPS, PULSE_RATE_BURST Per-caller rate limit, keyed by peer IP. Off unless PULSE_RATE_RPS is above zero. PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL The public origin, used for absolute URLs in the podcast feed. The feed refuses to render without it. APP_VERSION The version stamped on log lines. FEATURED_MESSAGES_PATH The file behind the featured-message strip. A2A_ORGANIZATION The organization named on the A2A agent card. Falls back to RUNINK_ORG, then CORE_GITHUB_ORG, then empty.
data.sign-in-and-users#Sign-in and users: Variable Effect PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD (or ADMIN_PASSWORD) Seeds the break-glass admin. Without it, no password login exists. PULSE_ADMIN_USERNAME, PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL Overrides the break-glass admin’s username (admin) and email. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID The Google OAuth client. Without it, Google sign-in is off. OIDC_ISSUER Overrides the token issuer that Google sign-in trusts. AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY true hides the password form. AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS The Google sign-in allowlist. Empty means nobody signs in with Google. AUTH_SEED_USERS Operator-granted roles as email=persona,…. Applied at every start. PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE, PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE The ClientInstance this deployment is. Lets the Admin page write member changes back to it. GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENDPOINT Used to refresh a Google integration’s access token for YouTube uploads. See Users and access.
data.site-audit-and-scoring#Site audit and sc: Variable Effect PULSE_SCORING_CONFIG A JSON file overlaid on the built-in scoring config. PULSE_AUDIT_CACHE_TTL How long an audit result is cached, in seconds. Default 3600. PULSE_PROSPECT_AUDIT_TIMEOUT Time limit for auditing one prospect’s site during lead prospecting. Go duration, for example 20s. PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL The site the daily audit engine checks. Falls back to PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL.
data.storage#Storage: Variable Effect PULSE_DB_PATH The SQLite file. Default ./pulse.db. PULSE_DATA_DIR Working data directory. Default ./data. PULSE_APPFS_BUCKET Bucket for the sealed app root (sessions, media, memo cache) on the object store. PULSE_APPFS_DIR Local sealed app root when there is no object store. Default $PULSE_DATA_DIR/appfs. OBJECTSTORE_ENDPOINT, OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET, OBJECTSTORE_ACCESS_KEY, OBJECTSTORE_SECRET_KEY The object store for the retrieval corpus and the app root. LITESTREAM_ENDPOINT, LITESTREAM_BUCKET, LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID, LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Litestream replication of the database.
data.telephony-and-messaging#Telephony and me: Variable Effect AUDIOSOCKET_ADDR The TCP listener Asterisk streams call audio to. ASTERISK_ARI_URL, ASTERISK_ARI_USER, ASTERISK_ARI_PASSWORD Asterisk’s REST interface, for placing calls. Leave empty to keep outbound calls off. ASTERISK_ENDPOINT_PATTERN, ASTERISK_CONTEXT, ASTERISK_EXTENSION, ASTERISK_CALLER_ID The dial string, dialplan target, and caller ID. CALLING_AGENT_URL The platform calling agent that carries browser voice calls. PULSE_WEBRTC_SIGNALING_ONLY true answers WebRTC offers locally for signaling tests. Such a call cannot hear the caller. TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER The WhatsApp and SMS edge. PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID Which user’s HubSpot connection backs the WhatsApp sender allowlist, and as whom replies run. SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS false turns automatic self-healing remediation off (plans are recorded only). Default: on. PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY false turns automatic WhatsApp/SMS replies off. Default: on. See Telephony and messaging.

data.backups-and-the-replica#Backups and the:
In a cluster, Litestream replicates SQLite to the in-cluster object store on the schedule in grpc/litestream.yml. The replica is plaintext at rest, including password hashes; see the comments in that file for the pending fix.
Once encrypted rows in the new envelope format exist, do not roll back to a build from before that format: it cannot read them.
data.health#Health:
GET /health always answers HTTP 200 with:
{"status":"ok","model_ready":false,"port":8080} The status code is deliberately unconditional. PULSE serves every non-AI feature without a model, so a readiness probe here should catch a wedged or unbound server, not an AI outage. Read model_ready for the model. It is true only when the engine is running and has confirmed it can serve a request.
data.licence-gate#Licence gate: With a licence configured (LICENSE or LICENSE_FILE, verified with LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY), every non-public call is refused with license expired or invalid when its signature is bad or it has expired. With no licence configured, nothing is gated.
data.logs#Logs:
Logs are OpenTelemetry-shaped JSON on stdout, with service.name pulse-backend and the version from APP_VERSION. Lines worth watching:
Log line Meaning refusing to start: ... A fatal startup condition. The rest of the line names it. AUTHENTICATION DISABLED — every request will be rejected as Unauthenticated The session key is one that authz refuses. Fix PULSE_JWT_SECRET. PUBLISHCFG ... What each outward channel is allowed to do grounding ACTIVE / grounding INACTIVE: Whether retrieval grounding works gRPC reflection ENABLED Reflection is on. It should not be on a deployed instance. security config validated, or a warning listing problems The result of the production gate
data.rate-limiting#Rate limiting: PULSE_RATE_RPS and PULSE_RATE_BURST cap calls per peer IP. Over-limit calls get ResourceExhausted before any other work. Off by default.
data.self-healing#Self-healing:
An in-process watchdog probes local resources and the inference and voice endpoints, and a remediator reacts to what it finds. SelfHealService/GetStatus shows it working: whether the loop is healthy, the last event, recent events, and how many remediations were tried and failed. healthy is false only when the most recent event is critical and was not remediated. The service only observes. It never triggers remediation itself.
Remediation is automatic by default, from a fixed list of non-destructive actions: restart one of PULSE’s model runners, add bounded capacity to one, open the in-process circuit breaker, roll back the loop’s own most recent change to a runner when that change was made shortly before the fault, or notify. A plan outside that list or below the confidence floor becomes a notification. Nothing deletes data, rolls back a release, or touches a security control. See the self-healing operations agent card.
To turn automatic remediation off, set SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS=false. Plans are still reasoned and recorded, but none is applied.
data.the-production-gate#The production gate:
At startup PULSE checks for insecure configuration:
The session key is missing or refused. CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset or contains a wildcard, while the app is not served same-origin through PULSE_WEB_DIR. With PULSE_ENV=production, any problem stops the server with refusing to start in production. Otherwise it is a warning.
PULSE_ENV is not set by any manifest today, so deployments run the warning path. Confirm the checks pass before you set it, or the pod will refuse to start. Reflection no longer depends on it: it has its own opt-in, PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION.
data.tls#TLS:
Pick one:
Setup How TLS at the edge (usual) Nothing to set. The edge terminates TLS and speaks plain HTTP to PULSE. Direct exposure PULSE_TLS_CERT and PULSE_TLS_KEY. TLS 1.2 minimum, forward-secret AEAD suites only. Service-plane mutual TLS MESH_MTLS=true, with the mesh CA. Every client needs a mesh certificate. TLS 1.3 only. If the CA is unavailable, the server refuses to start rather than downgrade.

data: PULSE is sold on its own, with its own plans. A PULSE subscription does not include FACE, and a FACE subscription does not include PULSE. PULSE charges per seat, plus compute on the Lite plan. It has no per-action or outcome fees.
data.compute-units#Compute units:
A compute unit (CU) is one second of model-slot time: the time a request holds the model while it generates. 3,600 CU is one slot-hour.
Lite includes 10,800 CU per seat per month, which is 3 slot-hours. The allowance is pooled: a 5-seat account has 54,000 CU to share. Past the allowance, Lite is billed $0.10 per 100 CU, in whole blocks of 100 CU. Work is never refused for going over. Dedicated and Enterprise are unmetered. The Billing page shows them as “unmetered”, never as a number, and they are never billed overage.
data.currency-and-billing-periods#Currency an: There is one US-dollar price list. You are invoiced in your regional currency, converted with the European Central Bank euro reference rates. The rate for a month is the last ECB publication before the 1st. It stays fixed for the whole month. Seat prices round to a whole unit of your currency. Overage and fees round to the currency’s smallest unit. Billing periods run from your subscription’s start date (anniversary periods), not from the calendar month. For how the numbers reach the Billing page of a deployment, see Billing.
data.how-pulse-records-compute#How PULSE reco: The model router measures the slot time of every generation and returns it with the response. PULSE records that exact figure, in milliseconds. Conversion to CU happens once, on the total for the period. Each record goes to the account that pays for the work, resolved from the signed-in person’s verified session. On an instance shared by several customers, each customer’s usage stays on that customer’s account. Each record carries an idempotency key, so a retried write never counts twice. A generation whose slot time was not measured records nothing, and is counted in pulse_metering_unmeasured_total. PULSE never estimates a charge. Work that cannot be tied to a paying account is recorded under the platform account, which is never billed. Each case writes an audit line and is counted in pulse_metering_unattributed_total.
data.plans#Plans:
Plan Where PULSE runs Seats Price per seat per month Compute units Lite Runink’s shared hardware, spot-style 1 to 9 $49 billed yearly, or $59 month-to-month 10,800 CU per seat per month, pooled across the account Dedicated Runners in your own cloud: Google Cloud, Databricks, or Snowflake 10 or more $99, billed yearly Unlimited Enterprise Your premises or your own cloud 10 or more Custom quote Unlimited Prices are the US-dollar list. See Currency and billing periods for how your invoice is priced.
Lite runs in the spare capacity of Runink’s shared hardware, the way spot capacity works on a public cloud. That is why it is the lowest price, and why it is the only plan that meters compute.
Dedicated runs PULSE’s work on runners in your own cloud account. The compute is on your cloud bill, so it is not metered in compute units. Runink adds a fee of 1% of those runners’ cloud cost. There is no node fee.
Enterprise is quoted to fit the deployment. On-premises runners carry no runner fee.

data: PULSE drafts a great deal on its own: daily social copy, blog posts, podcast episodes, videos. Whether any of it leaves the building is decided by two layers of switches, and nothing is armed by default.
data.channel-specific-safeguards#Channel-spec: Channel Also needs blog A GitHub data source with a token, and PULSE_SITE_REPO. youtube YOUTUBE_PRIVACY_STATUS. Unset means private, so an unreviewed upload is never public by accident. linkedin LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN from a secret (never from the database) and LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN for a person. Organization pages are refused. podcast, audiobook PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, and the episode’s audio must exist. Then submit /podcast/feed.xml once to each podcast platform.
data.checking-what-is-armed#Checking what is:
At startup the server logs one line per channel:
PUBLISHCFG youtube: armed=false (...); channel opinion from ...; console config: ... A refused publish logs PUBLISHCFG : DISARMED — did NOT ..., with the layer that decided.
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=yes, on, 1, or TRUE does not arm anything. The server warns at startup with PUBLISHCFG-AMBIGUOUS. Write exactly true.
data.setting-a-channel#Setting a channel:
A channel’s own setting comes from the first of these that holds a clear yes or no:
An environment variable, PULSE_PUBLISH_, for example PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE=false. It accepts 1, t, true, y, yes, on and 0, f, false, n, no, off. A config file, at PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH (default /etc/runink/pulse-publishing.json), or the same JSON inline in PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON when there is no file. The built-in default, which is on. Combined with a kill switch that is off by default, nothing publishes until someone arms the global. The config file accepts either shape:
[{"channel": "youtube", "armed": false}] {"channels": [{"channel": "youtube", "armed": false}]} A channel missing from the file has no opinion. A file that cannot be read or parsed is ignored and changes nothing in either direction.
data.the-channels#The channels: Channel key What it publishes blog A Hugo post on your website, through GitHub. See Site pipeline. podcast Podcast episodes, by adding them to the public RSS feed audiobook The weekly long-form book, in the same feed youtube Real uploads to a YouTube channel, under the operator’s Google identity linkedin Text posts on one personal LinkedIn profile instagram Nothing yet. data.the-rule#The rule: armed(channel) = PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is exactly "true" AND the channel's own setting is on PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is the kill switch. It is off unless it is exactly the lowercase string true. When it is off, no channel can publish, whatever else is set. Each channel can then be narrowed. A channel with no setting of its own follows the kill switch. A channel setting can only turn a channel off. It can never turn one on when the kill switch is off.
data.the-same-switch-gates-server-writes#The: PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true is also what allows the Site Audit’s apply modes (apply, commit, pr) to write to the server’s filesystem and run git, and what arms the daily blog drafting in the social engine.
data.what-disarming-does-to-queued-posts#What:
The kill switch applies at the moment of publishing, not only when a post is queued. A scheduled post that comes due on a disarmed channel is marked withheld, with the reason. That is final. Re-arming does not replay the backlog; schedule the content again to re-queue it.
Approving content does not bypass the switch either. An approval is consent to the content, and the switch is a statement about the channel.

data: PULSE can run a company website’s content loop end to end: it writes blog posts and publishes them to the site’s Hugo repository, audits the live site every day, and opens pull requests that fix what the audit finds. Runink runs its own site this way. Each deployment points PULSE at its own site. There are no defaults that name Runink.
data.audit-fix-pull-requests#Audit-fix pull r:
From a relevance audit report, a person can apply the fix artifacts to a site repository (ApplyAuditActions). See Apply the fixes.
plan is a dry run and always allowed. apply, commit, and pr need PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and a signed-in caller. In pr mode with a GitHub connection, PULSE opens the pull request against the connection’s owner and repo, on branch seo/pulse-remediation by default, against main. Copy and infrastructure changes are returned as manual and never applied.
data.how-a-post-gets-there#How a post gets th: A post is written. Either the social engine drafts one blog article per active campaign per day, or you approve blog-channel content yourself. It is scheduled. The social engine schedules its draft two hours ahead. That window is a chance to cancel it on the Schedule screen before the worker dispatches it. It is published over git. PULSE renders the content as a Hugo post at /.md and, by default, opens a pull request on branch pulse/publish-. Nothing goes live until someone merges it. No third-party social API is involved. The post goes to your own repository with your own GitHub token.
data.settings#Settings: Variable Default Meaning PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED off Must be exactly true. PULSE_PUBLISH_BLOG follows the global Set false to silence only the blog. PULSE_SITE_REPO none, required owner/repo of your site. PULSE_SITE_BRANCH main Base branch. PULSE_SITE_BLOG_DIR content/blog Where posts go. PULSE_SITE_PUBLISH_MODE pr pr opens a pull request. commit pushes to the base branch and is live at once. PULSE_SITE_AUTHOR omitted The author in the post’s front matter. PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL omitted Your site’s base URL, used for the canonical link. The GitHub token comes from the GitHub connection of the user who owns the content. See Connections.
data.the-daily-site-audit#The daily site audi:
Once a day, at 03:47 UTC, the site audit engine runs the relevance audit against one URL and stores the full report. It also files a readable digest as content on the site_audit channel. That channel is not publishable: the digest exists to be read.
Variable Meaning PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL The site to audit. PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL Used when PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL is unset. With neither set, the engine does not start and logs Site Audit Engine: NOT started — no target site; set PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL (or PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL).
The first audit after a deploy waits for the next 03:47 UTC slot. Run one on demand from Site Audit at any time. Each audit is limited to 10 minutes. A run that scored nothing, for example because the site was unreachable, is recorded as a failure rather than a result.
The engine audits and records. It never fixes. Fixing stays a human decision.
data.when-it-refuses#When it refuses: Message Cause website publishing is disabled: ... The blog channel is not armed. The message names the layer that decided. no github integration/token configured for user ... The content’s owner has no GitHub connection. PULSE_SITE_REPO is not set — refusing to publish; set it to YOUR site repo as owner/repo No target repository. invalid site repo "...": expected owner/repo The repository is malformed. refusing to publish empty content The post has no title or body. The daily blog drafting only runs while the blog channel is armed. A disarmed channel costs no model time.

data: PULSE has three voice and messaging paths. All three are off until you configure them.
data.browser-voice-calls#Browser voice calls:
The app’s full-screen call view sends a WebRTC offer to /voice/webrtc/offer. PULSE forwards it to the platform’s shared calling agent at CALLING_AGENT_URL, which carries the audio. PULSE is only the authenticated signaling door.
When CALLING_AGENT_URL is unset, the offer is refused with HTTP 503 and voice calling is not configured: CALLING_AGENT_URL is unset. PULSE’s own local handler cannot decode audio, so it no longer pretends to connect. PULSE_WEBRTC_SIGNALING_ONLY=true turns that local handler back on for signaling tests only; the caller will not be heard.
Turn-based voice input (/voice/transcribe) needs only the Voxtral server (VOXTRAL_REMOTE_URL). Both voice endpoints require a signed-in caller.
data.outbound-calls-to-leads-asterisk#Outboun:
Leads → Call (LeadService.CallLead) places a real phone call through a self-hosted Asterisk PBX. There is no per-minute calling SaaS.
PULSE asks Asterisk’s REST interface (ARI) to dial the lead into a dialplan context. That context runs AudioSocket() back to PULSE’s audio listener, passing the call’s ID: AudioSocket(${PULSE_CALL_ID},:8199). PULSE sets PULSE_CALL_ID on every call it places. The ID is how a call finds its own cold-call script; without it the call runs with no script. PULSE transcribes the caller (Voxtral), answers with the sales agent, speaks the reply (Runink TIDE’s shared ttsd, TTSD_URL), and streams it back. Variable Meaning AUDIOSOCKET_ADDR The TCP listener Asterisk connects to ASTERISK_ARI_URL, ASTERISK_ARI_USER, ASTERISK_ARI_PASSWORD ARI access. Leave empty to keep outbound calls off. ASTERISK_ENDPOINT_PATTERN The dial string, with {number} substituted ASTERISK_CONTEXT, ASTERISK_EXTENSION The dialplan target that runs AudioSocket() ASTERISK_CALLER_ID Outbound caller ID If ARI is configured and the audio listener cannot bind, the server refuses to start. Otherwise it would place calls it cannot carry: the lead would answer to silence. When ARI is not configured, a failed bind is only a warning.
Without ARI, CallLead returns outbound calling isn't configured — set up Asterisk and ..., naming the missing variables.
Outbound cold calling is regulated. Consent, calling hours, do-not-call lists, and recording disclosure are the operator’s responsibility.
data.whatsapp-and-sms#WhatsApp and SMS:
PULSE accepts inbound WhatsApp and SMS messages from Twilio at /twilio/message, and answers with its marketing personas: the same set it offers over A2A.
Every request must carry a valid Twilio signature (TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN). Only senders who are contacts in PULSE’s HubSpot account may talk to it. PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID picks whose HubSpot connection is used. The default is to deny. The edge only generates text: analysis, content, strategy, research. It cannot create leads or campaigns or approve content. Those stay behind the signed-in gRPC API. Replies are automatic and on by default. Each one passes PULSE’s guardrails: the incoming message is treated as data, never as instructions; a message that tries to override the agent is refused with a fixed reply and never reaches the model; and the reply is screened before it is sent. Replies run as the user set in PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID; with none set, nothing is answered. To turn automatic replies off, set PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY=false. Messages are then received but not answered. Variable Meaning TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN The Twilio account TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER The WhatsApp sender and the SMS number PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID The user whose HubSpot contacts form the allowlist, and as whom replies run PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY false turns automatic replies off. Default: on

data: PULSE keeps its own accounts in the users table. Each account has one role: admin, editor, or viewer. There are three ways an account comes to exist.
data.google-sign-in#Google sign-in:
Set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID to turn on Sign in with Google, and set AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS to the people allowed to use it. Google sign-in fails closed:
Situation Result GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset No Google button. The exchange endpoint answers google sign-in not configured (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset). Allowlist empty Nobody signs in with Google. The user sees google sign-in is not available on this instance. Email not on the allowlist Refused with this account is not authorized for this instance. First sign-in of an allowed email A new viewer account with an unusable random password. Set AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY=true to hide the password form. The break-glass admin still exists, but the app no longer shows the form to reach it.
data.seeded-roles#Seeded roles:
AUTH_SEED_USERS grants roles by email, as a comma-separated list of email=persona pairs. Runink TIDE’s operator projects it from the ClientInstance’s user list. It is applied at every start.
Persona Role admin, org_admin, owner admin writer, editor editor reader, viewer viewer An unknown persona grants nothing, and the entry is skipped with a warning. A seeded email that has no account yet gets one with an unusable password, so that person signs in with Google.
data.sessions#Sessions:
Sessions live in the sealed app root, not in the database, so every replica sees the same state.
An access token lasts 24 hours. A refresh token lasts 7 days and works once. A session lasts at most 30 days. Signing out revokes the session and every token issued in it. The Account page can end all of a person’s sessions on every device. Tokens issued before server-side sessions existed carry no session ID and are refused. Those users sign in again once.
data.the-admin-page#The Admin page:
Admins see Admin in the navigation (/admin). It is the shared Runink members page (runink.ui.access.v1.AccessService): list members, invite, change a role, remove. The server reads the caller’s role fresh from the users table on every call, not from the token, and refuses anyone who is not an admin of this instance.
What a change does depends on where the roster lives:
Deployment What happens to a change PULSE may patch its own ClientInstance (PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE is set and the pod has permission) Written to the ClientInstance first, then to the users table. It is pending until the operator re-projects the roster and PULSE restarts. AUTH_SEED_USERS is set, but PULSE cannot write the ClientInstance Refused, with a sentence saying where access is changed. A local change would be undone at the next start. Neither The users table is the roster. Changes apply at once. When a role changes, PULSE ends that person’s sessions, so the new role takes effect at their next sign-in. PULSE keeps no seat roster, so invites are not limited by the number of seats on the subscription.
PULSE serves one instance per deployment. Its ID is PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE, else TENANT_ID, else pulse.
data.the-break-glass-admin#The break-glass ad:
When PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD is set, the server creates or updates an account named admin with the admin role at every start. Change the username or email with PULSE_ADMIN_USERNAME and PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL.
Without the variable, the log says No admin password injected (PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD/ADMIN_PASSWORD unset) — skipping admin seed; break-glass login unavailable until one is provided.
This is an emergency account. Give it a strong password from the secret store, and use Google sign-in and seeded roles for everyday access.

data:
PULSE’s API is gRPC. The contracts are the .proto files in grpc/api/proto/pulse/v1/: pulse.proto, activity.proto, and commons.proto, in package pulse.v1. Browsers use gRPC-Web on the same port.
There is no REST API, no webhook registration, and no client library besides the generated stubs (Go in grpc/api/v1/, Dart in flutter/lib/core/grpc/). The few plain HTTP routes are listed under HTTP endpoints .
To call the API, see Calling the API.

Route Auth Purpose GET /health None Always 200. The Data sources tab. PULSE serves it over its own integrations table and narrows the catalog to HubSpot and GitHub.
Method Purpose ListConnectionTypes The connector types offered: HubSpot and GitHub ListConnections, ListConnectionNames, GetConnection Read your connections CreateConnection, UpdateConnection, DeleteConnection Manage them RotateCredentials Replace the stored token TestConnection Check the token against the platform A connection that sets a runner, an environment, or properties is refused, and nothing is stored.

PULSE has no platform admin, so the page does not show that row.
